The core abstraction treats each file in a partition as a node in a directed graph of claims, where edges represent logical dependencies or contradictions. Each claim is classified via a deterministic function of its supporting evidence, mapped to one of five dispositions. The system enforces full-read compliance through a recursive traversal protocol that ensures no claim is skipped or duplicated. A key duality emerges: the distinction between claims that are implemented (in the main repo) versus those that are only accessible via calibrated boundaries. This duality enables a layered reasoning architecture where claims can be evaluated under different epistemic constraints depending on their boundary state. Failure modes include misclassification due to ambiguous evidence, or incomplete traversal when files are unreadable. The system's robustness depends on maintaining consistent symbolic representations of claims and their dispositions across all layers of abstraction.
